conventions.convention: BY takes m ≥ 1 and q ∈ (0,1), uses c_k = kq/(mH_m), orders ties by original index, and rejects the first R ranks for the largest passing rank, with R = 0 when none passes.
The partition lemma requires 0 < c_1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ c_m ≤ 1, sets y_(0) = 0, and interprets the zero-coordinate product as the singleton empty tuple with its full sigma-algebra.

PRDS requires, for each designated true-null coordinate, one conditional-law kernel whose evaluations on every increasing Borel set are nondecreasing on the entire marginal support. Borel means the finite product of trace Borel structures; the empty true-null set gives a vacuous condition.
The standard-Borel regular conditional-law interface assumes AC; the BY proof and deterministic partition are choice-free.

The testing family is fixed before observing data. Validity is superuniformity under the corresponding null laws, including vacuous validity for empty nulls. FDR is E[V/(R ∨ 1)], giving zero FDP when R = 0.

load_bearing.statement: For m ≥ 1 and 0 < c_1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ c_m ≤ 1, {I_i = 1, R = k} = {p_i ≤ c_k} ∩ {p_-i ∈ C_i,k}. The C_i,k form a disjoint Borel partition of the remaining-coordinate space. D_i,k = ⋃_{j≤k} C_i,j is coordinatewise increasing and Borel, with D_i,m the whole space; for k < m it equals ⋂_{r=k}^{m−1}{y_(r) > c_(r+1)}.
The law of P is PRDS on I_0 if, for each i ∈ I_0, a conditional-law version K_i can be chosen so that x ↦ K_i(x,D) is nondecreasing on supp(μ_i) for every coordinatewise increasing Borel set D.
Let P = (P_1,…,P_m) be p-value random variables, m ≥ 1, q ∈ (0,1), and i ∈ I_0. If P_i is valid under this law and P is PRDS on I_0, then BH at level q satisfies E[I_i/(R ∨ 1)] ≤ q/m.

For a statistical experiment and a fixed finite family of m ≥ 1 null hypotheses with p-value statistics valid for their respective nulls, BY satisfies FDR_θ ≤ (m_0(θ)/m)q ≤ q for every q ∈ (0,1), without a dependence condition.

Assume AC. For a statistical experiment and a fixed finite family of m ≥ 1 null hypotheses with p-value statistics valid for their respective nulls, if under every P_θ the vector is PRDS on I_0(θ), ordinary BH satisfies FDR_θ ≤ (m_0(θ)/m)q ≤ q for every q ∈ (0,1).
Let I = [0,1] with the subspace topology from the usual real topology and with its Borel sigma-algebra. Then (I, B(I)) is a standard-Borel space.
